hook: *₹50 crore* lost to 'digital arrest' scams this year
hook_b: *₹50 crore* lost to 'digital arrest' scams this year
tldr: The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau got 846 digital arrest complaints from January to October 2026; police filed 241 FIRs.

beats.what: Fraudsters pose as police, CBI or ED officers with fake warrants and keep victims on video calls, sometimes for days.
beats.why: Since January 2024 Telangana has logged 5,097 such complaints with ₹320 crore lost.
beats.care: No real agency arrests anyone over a video call; calls about a 'parcel with drugs' are a known opening line.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Average monthly losses dropped to ₹5 crore this year from ₹14.7 crore in 2024.

cards.q: Has anyone you know got a fake 'police' or 'parcel' call?

qs: Why is each victim losing more even as complaints fall?
How much of the ₹50 crore has been recovered?

facts.t: Since Jan 2024 Telangana has recorded *5,097* digital arrest complaints and *₹320 crore* in losses.
Average loss per complaint is *₹5.9 lakh* in 2026, vs ₹5.8 lakh in 2024.

viz.verdict: Fewer people are reporting these calls each month.
Monthly losses are down, but each victim loses more on average.

learn.t: Digital arrest = a scam where callers pretend to be officials and 'arrest' you over video call to extort money

watch: Whether the per-complaint loss keeps rising even as cases fall.

fact: Telangana lost *₹50 crore* to 'digital arrest' scams in 10 months
twist: Complaints fell to *85 a month* from 253 in 2024, yet the average loss per complaint rose to ₹5.9 lakh.
